(Brief Minutes of the Meeting Proceedings)
Wednesday, Ashar 31, 2083
The meeting of the House of Representatives commenced today at 1:24 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal.
At the commencement of the meeting, as Honourable Members from Nepali Congress, Communist Party of Nepal (UML), Communist Party of Nepal, Shram Sanskriti Party, and Rastriya Prajatantra Party sought time to speak by standing in front of their seats, the Right Honourable Speaker granted them time. They expressed their views on various issues, stating that the daily events in the country are increasing despair rather than hope; the style of diverting issues by covering them with stunts has become outdated; the statement made by the Right Honourable Prime Minister needs to be retracted from the floor of the House and removed from the parliamentary records; the government is remaining silent even as the citizenship of citizens is changing due to border pillars; the army had to be mobilized for border defense; the government needs to be serious about resolving the landless problem; the government is overly focused on populist and publicity-oriented activities, which are leading the country towards destruction; the rule of law must be implemented; bank loans are a major factor in the self-immolation of youth; the arrest of Majid Ansari needs to be investigated, among other issues.

Following this, during the impromptu session, the following Honourable Members raised their concerns: the condition of the Mechi Highway in Ilam and other alternative road sections is dire, and the government's attention is needed; the removal of landless people is creating problems, and the issue needs to be resolved; the immediate reconsideration of recruiting contract and daily wage workers through contractors is necessary; in the case of 2-year-old Ashish Bhandari in Dolpa, Baglung district, who died on the spot after being trapped by a landslide, heartfelt condolences are offered to the deceased and deep sympathy to the family; Mina Karki of Gulmi went missing while crossing the Resa River in Baglung, and efforts should be intensified in the search; the incident of self-immolation by Gautam Kumar Sahani of Rautahat expresses despair towards the government; due to a problem with the server of the Central Transport Office, transport services in Itahari have been obstructed, and the government needs to resolve this issue; in Goljor Rural Municipality, Sindhuli, a landslide on Ashar 28 buried local Hem Bahadur Dura Magar along with his house, and due to road obstruction during rescue efforts, timely rescue and treatment were delayed, indicating that most roads in hilly areas are similar; therefore, the government must promptly carry out all activities from disaster risk preparedness to response and management, including relocating residents in disaster-prone areas; services at Bir Hospital, Teaching Hospital, and Gangalal Hospital are affected due to a shortage of medicines; health services beneficiaries are unable to receive payments due to medical mafias; heartfelt condolences are offered to Bishnu Thapa of Baglung, who lost his life in a gas cylinder explosion in the Baudha-Jorpati area, and Hemkala Bhandari, who lost her life due to electrocution, and deep sympathy is expressed to the bereaved families, urging that appropriate relief and compensation be provided to the affected families of both incidents; to address the growing mental health problems in the country, a Mental Health Council should be formed immediately; furthermore, as mental health services are limited, unequal, and capital-centric, the old policy should be revised and a new policy formulated; settlements are at risk of flooding due to the rise in Lal Bakaiya and Bagmati rivers in Rautahat; it is the moral responsibility of the Prime Minister to answer the questions raised in Parliament; the government is talking about digital governance, but problems with the servers of the Department of Transport Management and the Department of Land Management and Records have halted services across the country, necessitating the government to build reliable digital infrastructure; an Internal Revenue Office should also be established in West Nawalparasi district, among other issues.

Subsequently, Honourable Ain Bahadur Mahar, from the parliamentary party of the Communist Party of Nepal (UML), expressed his views on contemporary issues.
Subsequently, Honourable Aaren Rai, from the parliamentary party of the Shram Sanskriti Party, expressed his views on contemporary issues.
Subsequently, Honourable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, stated that the government will introduce 64 bills in the Federal Parliament by the end of Kartik and 166 bills within the next year, and that policy reforms to facilitate service delivery are a government priority.
Thereafter, the Right Honourable Speaker read out the following letter received from the Office of the President:

Thereafter, Honourable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda', presented the "Eighteenth Annual Report of the National Human Rights Commission FY 2081/082", "Annual Report of the National Information Commission FY 2081/082", and "Seventh Annual Report of the National Inclusion Commission FY 2081/082" to the House, respectively.
Following this, the Right Honourable Speaker informed about a minor change in the day's agenda.
Subsequently, the proposal moved by the Honourable Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment, Ramji Yadav, "Let the provisions of Protocol No. 29 of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930 (No. 29) of the International Labour Organization be discussed in the House" was presented for decision and unanimously approved.

Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker presented the proposal "Let the Bill to Amend and Repeal Some Nepal Laws Related to Finance, 2083 be considered" for decision, and it was unanimously approved.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker informed that Honourable Members wishing to register amendments to the "Bill to Amend and Repeal Some Nepal Laws Related to Finance, 2083" in accordance with Rule 112 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, can register them at the Bill Section (House of Representatives), Federal Parliament Secretariat, Singhdarbar.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker stated that during the Second Session of the House of Representatives, 2082, important bills including the Appropriation Bill, 2083, Finance Bill, 2083, and Public Debt Raising Bill, 2083, were passed along with the government's annual policy and program; it is the primary responsibility of the members of the House of Representatives to listen to and understand public feedback, concerns, and suggestions regarding the state's policies and programs implemented, laws formulated, and service delivery by the end of the current fiscal year; in line with the constitutional principle that the relationship between the federal, provincial, and local levels shall be based on cooperation, coexistence, and coordination, and the constitutional spirit, the members of the House of Representatives should also take a leading role in harmonizing development, lawmaking, and public service delivery among all three tiers and connecting the experiences, complexities, and expectations of provincial governments and local levels with the federal level; as Parliament is the center of democracy, the vibrancy of Parliament is determined by how close the MPs are to the people, and representatives also serve as a democratic bridge connecting the public and Parliament with trust, dialogue, and accountability. The essence of representation is the dual responsibility of bringing the voices, aspirations, and expectations of the people to the parliamentary decision-making process and re-establishing parliamentary decisions among the people. It is the fundamental parliamentary responsibility of every Honourable Member to continuously engage with the public, communicate with them, and reflect public opinion in the parliamentary process; recognizing the need for time for Honourable Members to reach their constituents and citizens for important work in further strengthening the relationship between all three tiers, connecting the public with the House, and preparing the ground for extensive debate on bills; the more robust the relationship between Parliament and the public, the more accountable, participatory, and trustworthy democracy becomes; the government has declared the upcoming fiscal year as the "Year of Lawmaking and Reform." Given the significant role of Parliament in this campaign of reviewing, amending, consolidating, and enacting necessary new laws, the Honourable Members will play an active role in the upcoming meetings. With this foresight and wishing that the adjournment of the parliamentary meeting be transformed into a discourse with the public, the meeting of the House of Representatives was adjourned at 6:35 PM, to reconvene on Thursday, Shrawan 14, 2083, at 11:00 AM.
Padma Prasad Pandey
Secretary General

Honourable members from various parties raised concerns about national issues including border security, landless problems, government populism, and youth self-immolation due to debt. They demanded accountability and policy changes.

sections.summary_en: Numerous Honourable Members spoke on various contemporary issues, including national development, social concerns, and government performance. The leaders of the CPN (UML) and Shram Sanskriti Party also presented their views.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Minister of Law announced plans for introducing numerous bills and policy reforms. The Speaker read out presidential authenticated bills. Reports from human rights, information, and inclusion commissions were presented. The House discussed and ratified two ILO conventions on forced labor and labor inspection, with the Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment responding to questions. The Finance Minister presented a bill to amend finance-related laws, which was discussed and approved.
